messages.subject: Error Encountered with morphol.disparity Function
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I am currently conducting research on morphological variations in triatomine bugs, specifically focusing on the heads and wings of resistant strains. I am reaching out to inquire about the possibility of comparing the Procrustes variances between two different sets of morphological structures and configurations of landmarks.

In the head structure, I have identified 5 morphological landmarks, while in the wing structure, there are 11 landmarks that I have considered for analysis.

My research aims to determine which of these structures exhibits greater variability, with a specific focus on understanding the morphological differences in resistant strains. To achieve this, I intend to utilize the morphol.disparity function. However, I encountered an error message stating: "Error: Variables or data might be missing from either the data frame or global environment, or a linear model fit just does not work..."

I would greatly appreciate your guidance on how to address this issue and whether it is feasible to compare the variances of Procrustes between these distinct morphological structures. Additionally, any insights or suggestions you can offer regarding the analysis would be invaluable to my research.

Thank you very much for considering my inquiry.

Below, I am providing the code I have been working on:

morphol.disparity(TGAHC.gdf$coords~TGAH.gdf$coords+TGAH.gdf$LID,
                  groups = TGAH.gdf$LID,
                  iter = 999)

Kind regards,
Federico.

messages.subject: Error "Data names and covariance matrix names do not match"
messages.subject_clean: Error "Data names and covariance matrix names do not match"
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I am hoping a member of this group knows how to overcome this error "Data names and covariance matrix names do not match" which is traced back to the .lm.rrpp function used by several other functions including lm.rrpp and procD.gls. My lab has code that worked previously with these functions but now gives us this error and any new attempts also give us this error. The name.check function in geiger confirms that the data and phylogeny names match. Does anyone have any insights as to what may be going on?

For example, we have the vcv matrix from the phylogeny reeftr (trvcv) and two traits (cp7 and sl), one of which is a factor (cp7) .

name.check(reeftr,cp7)
"OK"
name.check(reeftr,sl)
"OK"
trvcv<-vcv(reeftr)

rdf <- rrpp.data.frame(x = cp7, y = sl)
sl_allpat <- lm.rrpp(y~x, SStype="I", Cov = trvcv, data = rdf, iter= 999)

->"Error: Data names and covariance matrix names do not match"

Interestingly, if we don't use rrpp.data.frame and use the named vectors instead we get a slightly different error, which also traces back to the .lm.rrpp function

sl_allpat <- lm.rrpp(sl~cp7, SStype="I", Cov = trvcv, data = NULL, iter= 999)

-> "Error in dimnames(x) <- dn : length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent"

We get the same error if Cov=NULL as well.  Then to compound it, if we re-run the code using the rrpp.data.frame now we no longer get  "Error: Data names and covariance matrix names do not match" and instead get "Error in dimnames(x) <- dn : length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent". So the function is potentially being influenced by something from the R environment? This happens with different datasets and on different machines, so I feel like we are missing something simple!

Thanks - any help would be much appreciated!
Sam

messages.subject_clean: [geomorph-r-package] Error "Data names and covariance matrix names do not match"
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sam,

Can you indicate which versions of RRPP and geomorph you are using?  I could not replicate your errors with simulated data but I think this might have been something we already fixed.  An update would have to be installed via Github.  If you have version 2.0.0 of RRPP rather than 2.0.1, this might be the problem.  If this is not the problem, might there be some missing data?  I was able to produce a similar error if I changed one of the simulated data values to NA.  This would make sense because once the datum is removed, there are N - 1 data names despite N tree tip labels, even though the data frame had a slot for one taxon.  The name.check function still thinks things are okay because it only checks the labels, not the labels of data that are eventually used in the model fit.

Regarding the different errors, they are basically the same, but one message is because the problem eluded the established traps and triggered one of the default R error messages, instead.  The second error message though suggests the missing data option could be the problem.

Best,
Mike

messages.subject: Question regarding unsigned.AI from bilat.symmetry
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I’m trying to understand how the unsigned asymmetry index (‘unsigned.AI’) from ‘bilat.symmetry’ is calculated.

I have tried following the source code, however I am struggling with this section (lines 186 – 193):

###

unsigned.asymm <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(signed.asymm), ncol = ncol(signed.asymm))

for (i in 1:nrow(signed.asymm)) {

                                unsigned.asymm[i, ] <- ifelse(signed.asymm[i, ] %*% asymm.mean >

                                0, signed.asymm[i, ], signed.asymm[i, ] * (-1))

                }

###

>From what I understand, this section assigns the absolute value of the asymmetry component of each coordinate in the dataset (‘signed.asymm’ matrix) to the matrix ‘unsigned.asymm’.

However, when running the code, it seems that the asymmetry component of the first x value ‘x1’ of each sample is pasted along its entire corresponding row.

The unsigned asymmetry index is then calculated based on this matrix

Attached is an example performed in Geomorph 4.0.7, R v.4.3.3.

####

data(mosquito)

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(wingshape = mosquito$wingshape,

ind=mosquito$ind, side=mosquito$side,

replicate=mosquito$replicate) # make geomorph.data.frame

mosquito.sym <- bilat.symmetry(A = wingshape, ind = ind, side = side,

replicate = replicate, object.sym = FALSE, RRPP = TRUE,

iter = 499, data = gdf, print.progress = FALSE)

signed.asymm <- two.d.array(mosquito.sym$asymm.shape)

signed.AI <- sqrt(apply(signed.asymm^2, 1, sum))

asymm.mean <- apply(signed.asymm, 2, mean)

unsigned.asymm <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(signed.asymm), ncol = ncol(signed.asymm))

for (i in 1:nrow(signed.asymm)) {

                unsigned.asymm[i, ] <- ifelse(signed.asymm[i, ] %*% asymm.mean >

                0, signed.asymm[i, ], signed.asymm[i, ] * (-1))

    }

unsigned.AI <- sqrt(apply(unsigned.asymm^2, 1, sum))

#

I don’t understand why the asymmetry component of x1 should be repeated for every coordinate position, and why the unsigned AI should be calculated based solely on this value.

Any guidance on this matter is greatly appreciated.

Best regards,

Cecilia

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Question regarding unsigned.AI from bilat.symmetry
messages.body_plain:
Celia,

Thanks for your catch! Yes there was an error in that function, and it has been corrected. You may re-install from the Stable branch of github for the corrected version:

Install as:  devtools::install_github(“geomorphR/geomorph”, ref = “Stable”)

Note that the calculation of this index is precisely as described in Lazic et al. 2015: it is the square-root of the absolute value of the sum of squared deviations of R-L landmarks.  Because of this, there is no ‘signed.AI’ index equivalent. The reason is that the ‘signed’ component would be mathematically positivized in the squaring step, and would thus be redundant with the unsigned version (as such, signed.AI is now removed from bilat.symmetry as it is redundant with the corrected unsigned value).

Dean

messages.subject: Allometry: Visually significant predlines and insignificant pairwise tests.
messages.subject_clean: Allometry: Visually significant predlines and insignificant pairwise tests.
messages.body_plain:
Dear everyone,

I am having some issues understanding the results from my pairwise after carrying out an allometry analysis.

I read a couple of threads on the topic in this group and below is an answer that may make sense. Although, my sample size seems reasonable in my case. Therefore, I wonder if it is the way I use my codes which may cause these results. I am new to this kind of analysis and codes can be hard to understand. I would greatly appreciate it if somebody with a greater understanding than mine could help me understand these results 😊

A previous answer to this question:

„First, it is possible that one has a significant linear model effect with no pairwise comparisons being significant. This can occur in univariate anova-type models as well as multivariate models. Usually this boils down to power and sample size: in the aggregate there is enough signal to detect an effect, but broken down by pairs there is insufficient power to identify this (the alternative; a significant pairwise but not full anova is also possible, but for slightly different reasons).”

My codes:

### GDF with removed offshore and Unknown ###

# indices, tells which individuals to remove #

indices <- tursiopsBending.dt$spec$Sex != "Unknown" & tursiopsBending.dt$spec$State3 != "Offshore"

# Subset the array "tursiopsbending_sym.dt$symm.sh" along the third dimension using the indices. The third dimension represents the individuals #

tursiopsBending.dt$gpa.sh <- tursiopsBending.dt$gpa.sh[, , indices, drop = FALSE]

# Subset the individuals along "tursiopsbending_sym.dt$cs" #

tursiopsBending.dt$cs <- tursiopsBending.dt$cs[indices, drop = FALSE]

# Prepare the sex, ecotype and individual variables removing the unwanted individuals #

filtered_spec <- tursiopsBending.dt$spec[tursiopsBending.dt$spec$Sex != "Unknown" & tursiopsBending.dt$spec$State3 != "Offshore", ]

tursiopsBending.dt$spec <- filtered_spec

 # Produce the gdf #

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = tursiopsBending.dt$gpa.sh, sex = tursiopsBending.dt$spec$Sex, ind = tursiopsBending.dt$spec$LabID, Csize=tursiopsBending.dt$cs)

attributes(gdf)

### Allometry test on Sex only ###

fit.unique.Sex <- procD.lm(shape ~ log(Csize) * sex, data = gdf, iter = 9999) #unique

# Plot Predline #

plotAllometry(fit.unique.Sex, size = gdf$Csize, logsz = TRUE, method = "PredLine", pch = 19, col = color)

# Pairwise #

PW.allo.sex <-pairwise(fit.unique.Sex, groups = gdf$sex, covariate = log(gdf$Csize))

My results :

 Kind regards,

Morgane

messages.subject: Different results in PCA
messages.body_plain:
Dear everyone,

I just started working with GM, and due to my initial lack of confidence in conducting analyses, I opted to run them using different software to validate the results.

Initially, I measured my meshes using Meshlab and Slicer to ensure the accuracy of my scale. The dimensions of the individuals in both software programs closely matched those obtained with a caliper, affirming the correctness of the scale.

Subsequently, I utilized Checkpoint (Stratovan) to pplace my landmarks and exported the coordinates of my specimens at their original scale. This software suppose to export coordinates with the scale already incorporated, as indicated by the company's support team. However, upon conducting the Generalized Procrustes Analysis and PCA in two different softwares, MorphoJ and R (geomorph package), I encountered starkly divergent results.

Could anyone offer insight into what might be causing this disparity?

I thank you all in advance,

Best regards,

Bruno

Your email is unclear as to what precisely was different. Did you use different landmarking schemes in each analytical package for the PCA? Was it the same data in both packages for the PCA?  At what stage, and in what software, was GPA performed?

messages.subject: Understanding errors when comparing procD.pgls outputs
messages.subject_clean: Understanding errors when comparing procD.pgls outputs
messages.body_plain:
Dear All -

I'm encountering an error message when trying to compare outputs of the "procD.pgls()" function, and I'm hoping someone may be able to put me on the right track. Utilizing both the anova() and model.comparison() functions throw an error on my end. To recreate this:

******************
> data(plethspecies)
> Y.gpa<-gpagen(plethspecies$land)

Performing GPA
  |==============================================================================================================| 100%

Making projections... Finished!
> gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(Y.gpa, phy = plethspecies$phy)
> pleth.pgls <- procD.pgls(coords ~ Csize, phy = phy, data = gdf, iter = 999)

Please be aware that printing progress slows down the analysis (perhaps slightly).

Preliminary Model Fit...

Sums of Squares calculations: 1000 permutations.
  |==============================================================================================================| 100%
> pleth.null <- procD.pgls(coords ~ 1, phy = phy, data = gdf, iter = 999)

Please be aware that printing progress slows down the analysis (perhaps slightly).

Preliminary Model Fit...

Sums of Squares calculations: 1000 permutations.
  |==============================================================================================================| 100%

No terms for ANOVA; only RSS calculated in each permutation
> model.comparison(pleth.null, pleth.pgls, type = "logLik")
Error in sqrt(w) : non-numeric argument to mathematical function
> anova(pleth.null, pleth.pgls)
Error in sqrt(refModel$LM$weights) :
  non-numeric argument to mathematical function

*************************************

This does not seem to occur with OLS models:

*************************************
> pleth.Lm <- procD.lm(coords ~ Csize, data = gdf, iter = 999)
> pleth.nullLm <- procD.lm(coords ~ 1, data = gdf, iter = 999)
> model.comparison(pleth.nullLm, pleth.Lm, type = "logLik")
        logLik residual.pc.no <http://residual.pc.no> penalty       AIC
1     308.9513              8      88 -529.9027
Csize 119.6700              8     104 -135.3401
> anova(pleth.nullLm, pleth.Lm)

Sums of Squares calculations for 1 model: 1000 permutations.
  |==============================================================================================================| 100%

Analysis of Variance, using Residual Randomization
Permutation procedure: Randomization of null model residuals
Number of permutations: 1000
Estimation method: Ordinary Least Squares
Effect sizes (Z) based on F distributions

                  ResDf Df       RSS        SS        MS     Rsq      F       Z     P Pr(>F)
coords ~ 1 (Null)     8  1 0.0047685                     0.00000
coords ~ Csize        7  1 0.0041314 0.0006371 0.0006371 0.13361 1.0795 0.27376 0.395
Total                 8    0.0047685

*******************************

Based on the error messages, in both cases it looks like a missing argument that should be stored in "Model_Name$LM$weights" is to blame (I do see the printed message about ANOVA terms during the calculation of the null model, but I'm having this issue with more complex analyses as well).

Do I need to calculate/provide these weights manually to make such a comparison? Or perhaps I am missing a key concept in how GLS results should be compared and interpreted?

Thank you for your time and help, regardless!

Best regards,
~Ben

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Understanding errors when comparing procD.pgls outputs
messages.subject_clean: [geomorph-r-package] Understanding errors when comparing procD.pgls outputs
messages.body_plain:
Dear Ben,

There is an inherent problem with the anova.procD.lm and model.comparison functions to find some of the output it needs to do their jobs, which I will have to investigate.  This problem can be temporarily avoided, if you add verbose = TRUE as arguments to the model fits, e.g.,

pleth.null <- procD.pgls(coords ~ 1, phy = phy, data = gdf, iter = 999, verbose = TRUE)
pleth.pgls <- procD.pgls(coords ~ Csize, phy = phy, data = gdf, iter = 999, verbose = TRUE)

This assures all output is available.  I’ll have to see why the functions are not capable of generating the output when verbose = FALSE.  (Using verbose = FALSE means not appending a lot of results that are rarely used, a benefit when one has large data sets.)

Thanks for the alert!
Mike
